diagram_math_checks.objects: Four vertices (1,u), (1,v), (2,u), (2,v), with directed edges from time 1 to time 2; these are hidden-state instances, not morphisms.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Counterexample specifies S={u,v}, T=2 and y=(x,x); supplier Definition gives p(z,y)=pi(z1) B(z1,x) A(z1,z2) B(z2,x). All emissions equal 1.

diagram_math_checks.relation: u1→u2 has label 1; u1→v2 has dashed label 0; v1→u2 has label 34/65; v1→v2 has label 31/65.
diagram_math_checks.check: All four source-to-target pairs appear once, oriented left to right, exactly matching the two transition rows in the Counterexample. Diagonal crossing has no vertex and asserts no transition there. Row sums are 1 and (34+31)/65=1.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Path masses are uu=35/100, uv=0, vu=34/100, vv=31/100.
diagram_math_checks.check: Direct products: (7/20)·1=35/100; (7/20)·0=0; (13/20)·(34/65)=442/1300=34/100; (13/20)·(31/65)=403/1300=31/100. Sum is 1, so evidence is 1 and these also are posterior masses, as proved in 1.1.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Node marginal labels are (35/100,65/100) at time 1 and (69/100,31/100) at time 2.
diagram_math_checks.check: Time 1 row sums: 35+0=35 and 34+31=65. Time 2 column sums: 35+34=69 and 0+31=31, with denominator 100 throughout. Thus the unique marginal modes v1 and u2 are the two double circles, per 2.1.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Thick u1→u2 is the unique sequence MAP path; marginal-mode path vu is not MAP.
diagram_math_checks.check: 35>34>31>0, so uu has larger posterior mass than every other path, while the double-circled path vu has mass 34/100. The illustration only restates steps 1.1–2.1; their rigorous proof is untouched and independent.
